cold_open.hook: AMD down 8.75% as Wall Street suddenly remembers Jensen Huang's absence might actually matter.

markets.macro_note: Tech rotation away from chip plays; defensive names (META, PEP, KO) holding up as AI trade gets a reality check.

big_story.story_title: Jensen Huang's departure blasts big hole in AI startup funding, VCs and founders say
big_story.angle: Huang wasn't just Nvidia's CEO—he was the entire venture ecosystem's confidence anchor. Without him, the AI funding spigot doesn't just slow; it stops. What happens to the 200+ startups betting their Series B on his next move?

quick_hits.angle: Chip stocks cratering on the theory that Huang's departure means Nvidia's moat just got thinner—AMD, Broadcom, Avago all down hard. But the real question: is this repricing AI infrastructure as a commodity, or just panic selling?
FAA ground stop lifted after four hours, but the cancellation ripple will stretch into the weekend—travel chaos is the tax on whatever system failure just happened.
Lutnick's sons run a firm with deep Nvidia ties while he's Treasury Secretary—the optics are a minefield, and the Huang scandal just made it radioactive.
Fed survey says AI risks are now the top threat to financial stability—not rates, not inflation, not geopolitics. The system is officially spooked by something it doesn't fully understand.

odd_thing.joke_angle: Kalshi's CEO ditched Trump Jr. as an advisor because the 'optics weren't good'—which is the most polite way to say 'we hired a political celebrity and it immediately became a liability.'
